best_for: People with a folder of their own music files who want a clean, free player that sorts them by artist and album, on a Linux desktop or a Windows PC.

points.title: Built for your own files
points.text: Elisa browses a local music collection by genre, artist, album or track and builds playlists from it. It does not sell or stream music, so it suits a library you already own.

points.title: A few extras, kept simple
points.text: It can play online radio stations and show lyrics. Party Mode fills the window with album art. The goal is a calm player, not a tagger or a full library manager.

points.title: Fits in on Plasma
points.text: On the KDE Plasma desktop it follows your full color scheme. On other desktops and on Windows you get plain light and dark modes.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: Elisa is made by the KDE community and released under the LGPL-3.0. There is no account, no paid tier and no store inside it.

points.title: Windows and Linux builds differ
points.text: The Windows listing has one x64 installer, numbered 27.03.70, that can install for one user or the whole machine. The Linux Flatpak is at 26.08.3, is published by KDE and is verified on Flathub. Both pages list only one version, so older builds need another source.

points.title: No Mac version
points.text: KDE offers Elisa for Linux, Windows and Android, but not for macOS.
